text: |Moana Hugonot|STARSAILORS|Next Event :|SSL Gold Cup 2026|19 Nov - 13 Dec 2026|By Sailors For Sailors|News|Ranking|Global Ranking|Men Ranking|Women Ranking|Nations Ranking|Ranking Statistics|SSL Nation's Circuit|Rio 2026 - SSL Gold Cup|Sea Games|Events|Upcoming Events|Ongoing Events|Past Events|Media|About|Contact|Sign In|Menu|News|Ranking|SSL Nation's Circuit|Events|Media|About|Contact|Sign In|Ranking|Men Individual Ranking|Women Individual Ranking|Nations Ranking|Ranking Rules|Events|All Events|SSL Gold Cup|Battle of Nations (MTE)|About|Star Sailors League (SSL)|Sailing Athletes Foundation (SAF)|SSL Teams|FAQ|Contact|News|Shop|Sign in|Terms of Service|Privacy Policy|Follow us|Copyright © 2013 -|2026|Star Sailors League|All rights reserved.|Built by|SWATT Agency|.|Chat with us|Individual Ranking|skipper|crew|Moana|Hugonot|Rank|N/A|SSL Points|0|Country|TAHITI|Club|-|Height|175|cm|/|5’9”|Weight|85|kg|/|187|lbs|Bio|A Life Dedicated to the Ocean|Moana’s maritime journey began in 1987 aboard the famous training ship La Fleur de Lampaul, a foundational experience that defined his life's path. In 1989, he entered the fishing school at Île d'Yeu, gaining his first open-ocean experience on tuna trollers. Returning to Tahiti in 1993, he initially worked as a deckhand on new longliners arriving from Concarneau, crisscrossing every corner of Polynesia (Marquises, Tuamotu, Gambier, Australes) as well as the Cook and Kiribati islands. In 1996, he completed his military service in the French Navy aboard the patrol vessel La Tapageuse, a deployment that expanded his horizons to the Tonga and Niue islands. Following these diverse experiences, his leadership led him to become a captain from 2001 to 2017, commanding various tuna vessels ranging from 15 to 25 meters.|In 2017, Moana chose to transition his career, leaving commercial longline fishing in 2019 to bring his extensive expertise to the yachting industry. Relying on his vast sea time, he officially validated his skills in 2022, earning his Master 200 and Master 200 Sail captain's certificates along with all required safety modules. As a highly qualified skipper, he has mastered a wide variety of catamarans, including various Lagoon models (620, 43, 42, 40), Fountaine-Pajot yachts (Saba 50, Isla 40, Lucia 40, Tana 47), as well as the Excess 11.|Now based in Raiatea for the past three years, where he lives aboard, he initially worked with TradeWinds, catering to a predominantly American clientele. Today, he operates as a freelance professional skipper for Tahiti Yacht Charter. Highly trusted by his clients, he is currently completing a trans-Pacific delivery from Panama. This latest catamaran project was born from a partnership with a former client and investor, alongside Teva Pichard. Together, they are also preparing to represent Tahiti in the upcoming SSL Gold Cup qualifiers in Switzerland, where Moana will serve as a trimmer.|A devoted solo father to his two children, Kealohilani and Keahi, Moana beautifully combines a unique lifetime of maritime expertise, family devotion, and an unwavering passion for the seafaring life.|Records and Statistics|SSL Gold Cup|DATE|EVENT|CLASS|ROLE|RANK|2026|SSL Gold Cup 2026|Rio de Janeiro|,|BRAZIL|SSL 47|Crew|2|Statistics|TOTAL PODIUM FINISHES|Means the total number of times has finished a competition in the top 3 positions — 🥇 1st, 🥈 2nd, or 🥉 3rd place.|MEDAL RATE|Means the percentage of events or races where a person or team won a medal.|TOTAL EVENTS PARTICIPATED|Means the total number of competitions or races has taken part in — regardless of the result.|AVERAGE POINTS PER EVENT|Means the average number of points earns in each competition or race.|
